LESSON: PRONUNCIATION AND LISTENING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1.1: Pronunciation and Listening

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Pronunciation and Listening
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why should you listen keenly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. use vocabulary related to the theme in sentences correctly
2. use proverbs, fixed phrases, idioms, and metaphors with straightforward
3. listen for the main idea and specific details from an oral text

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Pronunciation and Listening

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Pronunciation and Listening

Teach
• Focus skill: use vocabulary related to the theme in sentences correctly.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Pronunciation and Listening.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Pronunciation and Listening
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should you listen keenly?
2. Why should you pronounce words accurately?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
